newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Sorceress saved kids in Colombia air crash-father.
newsitem.headline: Sorceress saved kids in Colombia air crash-father.

text.p: The father of two young children found alive after a plane crash in a remote jungle-covered area of northwest Colombia said on Tuesday that a sorceress was the key to their rescue.

The children, aged five and three, were rescued by helicopter along with their grandmother on Monday, five days after the small commuter aircraft in which they were travelling disappeared in a guerrilla-infested area of Choco province.
The children's mother died in the crash along with the plane's pilot and one other woman.

Ismael Aldana, the children's father and a former governor of Choco, told the Radionet news programme rescue workers had given up virtually given up hope of finding the plane when a relative suggested last Friday that he contact an Aruba-based fortuneteller, or sorceress, to seek her help.

First the woman, whom Aldana did not identify, suggested that he read her the names of various municipalities in and around Choco, Aldana said. Then she came up with the name of Bete, a small town on the Atrato River near the dense jungle where the downed aircraft, missing its wings and standing in a vertical position with its nose to the ground, was finally spotted by an aerial search-and-rescue team guided by Aldana.
"I don't know how she did it," he said, adding that the sorceress had worked nothing short of "a miracle."
